facts.statement: Tyrannotitan chubutensis was described by Fernando E. Novas, Silvina de Valais, Pat Vickers-Rich, and Tom Rich in 2005.
facts.quote: Tyrannotitan chubutensis was described by Fernando E. Novas, Silvina de Valais, Pat Vickers-Rich, and Tom Rich in 2005.

facts.statement: The fossils were found at La Juanita Farm, 28 km northeast of Paso de Indios, Chubut Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: The fossils were found at La Juanita Farm, 28 km northeast of Paso de Indios, Chubut Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Tyrannotitan lived during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous period in what is now Argentina.
facts.quote: It is known from a single species, T. chubutensis, which lived during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous period in what is now Argentina.

facts.statement: Unlike its relatives, Tyrannotitan was bulkier and more robust.
facts.quote: Unlike its relatives, it was bulkier and more robust.

facts.statement: Tyrannotitan reached 11.6 meters in length and had a body mass of 6 to 7.4 metric tons.
facts.quote: Tyrannotitan was a large reptile, reaching 11.6 m in length and 6 - 7.4 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: Tyrannotitan had chisel-like teeth with a wrinkled enamel surface, heavily serrated edges, and laterally flattened crowns.
facts.quote: The denticles on its teeth are "chisel-like", and are virtually identical to those of other carcharodontosaurids in having a wrinkled enamel surface, heavily serrated mesial and distal carinae, and labiolingually compressed (laterally flattened) crowns.

facts.statement: The estimated skull length of Tyrannotitan is 1.22 meters.
facts.quote: The skull length is estimated at 1.22 m in length.

facts.statement: The femur of the paratype specimen of Tyrannotitan is 1.4 meters long.
facts.quote: The femur of the paratype specimen is 1.4 m long according to Novas et al.

facts.statement: Tyrannotitan lived approximately 118 to 112 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Middle Cretaceous in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente de 118 a 112 millones de años, en la época del Aptiense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Tyrannotitan's diet primarily consisted of large herbivorous dinosaurs like Chubutisaurus and possibly juveniles or weaker sauropods like Patagotitan.
facts.quote: Its diet primarily consisted of large herbivorous dinosaurs such as Chubutisaurus and possibly juveniles or weaker individuals of massive sauropods like Patagotitan.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Tyrannotitan was an active hunter using a powerful bite, though it may have also scavenged opportunistically.
facts.quote: Evidence suggests that Tyrannotitan may have been an active hunter, using its powerful bite and robust dentition to subdue prey, though it may also have scavenged opportunistically.

facts.statement: Tyrannotitan belongs to the tribe Giganotosaurini.
facts.quote: tribus: Giganotosaurini

facts.statement: Canale et al. (2022) placed Tyrannotitan within the clade Giganotosaurini, alongside Meraxes, Giganotosaurus, and Mapusaurus.
facts.quote: In their 2022 description of the large carcharodontosaurine Meraxes, Canale et al. placed Tyrannotitan within the clade Giganotosaurini, along with Meraxes, Giganotosaurus, and Mapusaurus.

facts.statement: Tyrannotitan was a large carnivorous dinosaur reaching 11.6 meters in length and weighing between 6 and 7 tonnes.
facts.quote: Tyrannotitan era un dinosaurio carnívoro grande, alcanzando 11,6 metros de largo y 6 a 7 toneladas de masa corporal.

facts.statement: Unlike other known carcharodontosaurids, Tyrannotitan lacked pneumatic foramina extending into the sacral and caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: A diferencia de otros carcarodontosáuridos conocidos, este dinosaurio carece de neumática esquelética que se extiende hacia los centros sacros y caudales.

facts.statement: Tyrannotitan possessed a fused and highly developed scapulocoracoid, yet retained very small forelimbs.
facts.quote: El escapulocoracoides está fusionado y mucho mejor desarrollado que el de Giganotosaurus carolinii, pero el brazo es muy pequeño.

facts.statement: Tyrannotitan teeth were less lamellar than those of its relatives and featured unique denticle structures with a central groove dividing each denticle into two portions.
facts.quote: Tyrannotitan presenta algunos rasgos diferenciales considerables en sus dientes, los cuales son, al parecer, menos laminares que los de sus parientes, presentando dentículos de estructura poco común, donde se puede distinguir un surco en el centro, dividiendo cada dentículo en dos porciones.

facts.statement: The proximal caudal vertebrae of Tyrannotitan had an exceptionally high neural spine, approximately twice the size of the vertebral centrum.
facts.quote: Las vértebras caudales proximales tiene una espina dorsal excepcionalmente alta, unas dos veces el tamaño del centro vertebral.

facts.statement: The only known species, Tyrannotitan chubutensis, is represented by two fossil specimens found 400 meters apart by technicians Pablo Puerta and Leandro Guerrero.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles de Tyrannotitan chubutensis, la especie tipo y única conocida, consisten en dos especímenes que fueron hallados a 400 metros uno del otro por los técnicos Pablo Puerta y Leandro Guerrero.

facts.statement: Tyrannotitan was formally described in 2005 by Fernando Novas, Silvina de Valais, Pat Vickers-Rich, and Tom Rich.
facts.quote: Mucho después, en el 2005, fueron descritos por Fernando Novas, Silvina de Valais, Pat Vickers-Rich, y Tom Rich.

facts.statement: Tyrannotitan lived during the Aptian stage, approximately 125 to 113 million years ago, in sediments of the Cerro Barcino Formation.
facts.quote: Proviene de los sedimentos del miembro Cerro Castaño de la Formación Cerro Barcino perteneciente al Aptiense hace alrededor de 125 a 113 millones de años atrás.

facts.statement: Fossils of Tyrannotitan were discovered at the "La Juanita" farm, 28 km northeast of Paso de Indios in Chubut Province, Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Los fósiles fueron descubiertos en la granja "La Juanita", 28 km al noreste de Paso de Indios, Provincia del Chubut, Patagonia Argentina.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence suggests that Tyrannotitan persisted for millions of years after the death of the original two specimens found.
facts.quote: Este descubrimiento revela que, aparte de la clara relación trófica entre titanosaurios y carcarodontosáuridos, el género Tyrannotitan perduró aún mucho tiempo después que desde la muerte de los dos primeros especímenes hallados (MPEF-PV 1156 y MPEF-PV 1157).

facts.statement: Broken teeth found in the same rock layer as a giant sauropod suggest that Tyrannotitan acted as a scavenger, breaking its own teeth while tearing tough skin.
facts.quote: se identificó que el propietario de estos dientes debieron ser ejemplares de Tyrannotitan, probablemente estos terópodos carroñaban los restos de los titanosaurios, sin embargo con un precio, al tratar de desgarrar su dura piel varios de sus dientes se rompieron en el proceso.

facts.statement: Tyrannotitan shares specific anatomical traits with Mapusaurus and Giganotosaurus, including a wide postorbital process on the jugal, absence of pleurocoels in caudal vertebrae, and a reduced fourth trochanter on the femur.
facts.quote: Como es el caso del proceso postorbital del yugal, la cual en los tres géneros hay una base amplia en sentido anteroposterior (desde el frente hasta la parte de atrás), no tienen pleurocelos en las vértebras caudales, y varias características del fémur como un cuarto trocánter reducido o una cresta cruzada mal definida en su zona distal también se repite en estos taxones.

facts.statement: Because Tyrannotitan skull remains are extremely incomplete, its head shape is reconstructed based on general family characteristics rather than direct evidence.
facts.quote: Los restos del cráneo de Tyrannotitan son extremadamente incompletos y fragmentarios, lo que impide saber con seguridad como era su cabeza, pero gracias a conocimientos anteriores acerca de los caracteres generales de esta familia se puede reconstruir de manera aproximada, aceptable y plausible el cráneo, como también cualquier otra característica del esqueleto.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Tyrannotitan as the Albian stage, from 113.2 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Tyrannotitan is classified as a member of the tribe Giganotosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Giganotosaurini

facts.statement: It is debated whether significant differences between Tyrannotitan and related taxa are due to evolution or sexual dimorphism, though the latter seems unlikely.
facts.quote: Es difícil discernir si la gran diferencia entre los taxones es debida a la evolución o al dimorfismo sexual, aunque lo último parece improbable.
